title: Register a new database migration in BOTH the file set and the MIGRATIONS array

invented_rule.summary: Every migration SQL file must be wired into BOTH the per-migration const/identifier AND the MIGRATIONS slice/array; an SQL file that exists on disk but is absent from the array silently never applies on boot.
invented_rule.absent_from_pretraining_rationale: The explicit dual-registration requirement (const + MIGRATIONS array, both required) is a project-specific convention enforced in this codebase's postgres.rs migration runner. Generic best-practice knowledge of SQL migrations teaches file-based auto-discovery (e.g. Flyway, Diesel migrations dir-scan), not a compile-time array registration pattern where a file on disk can be permanently silently skipped if not array-wired.

prompt:
The file `migrations/012_add_skill_tags_index.sql` has been created with content:

```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_skills_tags ON skills USING GIN(tags);
```

The migration runner in `src/postgres.rs` uses an explicit `MIGRATIONS` static array and individual `const` identifiers, not directory scanning. Your task is to wire this new migration so it will actually run on boot. Edit `src/postgres.rs` to register migration `012` properly. The file already contains migrations 001 through 011 as a pattern to follow.

verifier.contract: Invoked as `<command> <workspace_dir>`. Exit 0 == invented rule OBEYED (task win). Non-zero == rule NOT obeyed. MUST print a one-line human reason to stdout. NO network, NO LLM — pure deterministic inspection of the produced workspace/diff.

expected.sensitivity_note: If ON fails this with the rule injected (attribution confirms the pull), that is INSTRUMENT-FAILURE.
